id.description: Permanent random id, reset only when state is wiped.

name.description: Display name, the hostname by default.

started.description: Whether the agent started working on it (see terminal.send).

turn.description: The turn when it went in (see terminal.send).

cwd.description: Its working directory now (resolved by the OS).

name.description: Its name as the OS has it (`node`, `vim`, `sh`).

current.description: Same build as the core: takes new terminals. Others drain.

key.description: The key sent: esc for programs that report status, else ctrl+c.

outcome.description:
stopped (left working, or a shell got its prompt back), exited,
still_working (no change in time), or unknown (it doesn't report status).

machines.description:
Machines added here and their lines: one that is not connected is
listed here, not waited on.

terminals.description: This machine's terminals, then each connected machine's (`machine/t7`).

MachineView.description: A machine as `machine ls` and `ls` show it: its profile and its line now.

host.description: What that core calls itself (its hostname).

name.description: What this core calls it: `rohan` in `rohan/t7`.

session.description: The hc session there (null: its default).

since_ms.description: Since when it is not connected (ms since the epoch).

target.description: How it is reached: an ssh target, or (`via`) a command.

temporary.description:
Short-lived (a sandbox for a task): clients may show it apart from the
machines that stay. hc treats it like any other.

version.description: Its hc version when last seen.

via.description:
`target` is a command that runs a shell line there, given as its last
argument, like ssh (a provider's own CLI, ssh with its options).

complete.description: False when part of what was asked for may be missing.

how.description: "screen", "history", or "stitched" (a full-screen app, read by scrolling it).

why.description:
Why only the screen: "working" (a full-screen app isn't scrolled while
it works; read again once it stops).

address.description: `t7`: this terminal forever on this core.

first_message.description: Template runs: whether the first message went in.

foreground.description: What runs in it right now and where (null once it has finished).

identity.description:
Which terminal the program believes it runs in (TERM_PROGRAM and
version), fixed at start; XTVERSION answers with it.

keep.description: Replace a lost program with this machine’s shell, in place. Exit with a code and kill remain final.

notify.description: Its parent gets notes about it (see `--no-notify`).

output.description:
With `wait`: its text then, like `terminal.read` (the screen, plus
history unless it is a full-screen app).

parent.description: The terminal that started it (`t3`), set once at start.

reason.description:
Why its program ended or is pending (`spawn_pending` means its initial
spawn timed out, but the holder may still be starting it):
exited, killed, server_stop, host_shutdown (Windows
is ending the session, including logout), signaled (a kept program
died by signal without an exit code), holder_lost (its holder
died), stopped_by_restart (nothing ran it any more after a restart).

records.description: Other 7501 records by id (programs reporting on several things).

reported.description: Whether the program ever sent a 7501 report.

rm.description: Removed right after it exits (once a waiting parent has the exit code).

screen.description: "exact", or "inexact" after a core crash (older history may be missing).

status.description:
The program's own word for what it's doing (OSC 7501 root record);
null if it never said, or after it exited.

status_ms.description: When that word last changed, ms since the epoch; null if it never said.

submit.description:
Template overrides: the key that submits a message, the stop key, the pause
between paste and submit.

turn.description: Goes up each time the status leaves `working`.

wait.description: With `wait`: how the wait ended (exit, a status, or timeout: still running).

started.description:
Whether it went `working` within a few seconds; null when it doesn't
report status, so nobody can tell.

status.description: The program's status word when the text went in (null: it never said).

turn.description: The turn when the text went in.

Status.description: One 7501 record. Words are the program's own; nothing is translated.

kind.description: permission, question or auth (blocked only, when the program said).

progress.description: 0..100 (working or blocked, when the program said).

state.description: idle, working, done, blocked or error.

holder.description: The holder new terminals go to.

holders.description: Every holder: after an update, older ones run their terminals to the end.

installed_by.description:
The package manager this hc came from (homebrew, nix, mise, or
system package manager): it updates hc, `hc update` won't.
Null for a replaceable plain install.

channel.description:
Framed mode: the channel events arrive on (JSON lines, with credit).
Plain mode: none; this connection now carries only notifications.

seq.description:
Events after this sequence follow. After a `missed` snapshot, ignore
events whose seq is not above the snapshot's.

terminals.description: Matching terminals here and on connected machines (`machine/t7`).

error.description: Set when the file can't be used.

address.description: `t7`: this terminal forever on this core.

foreground.description: What runs in it right now and where (null once it has finished).

Which terminal the program believes it runs in (TERM_PROGRAM and
version), fixed at start; XTVERSION answers with it.

spawn timed out, but the holder may still be starting it):
exited, killed, server_stop, host_shutdown (Windows
is ending the session, including logout), signaled (a kept program
died by signal without an exit code), holder_lost (its holder
died), stopped_by_restart (nothing ran it any more after a restart).

records.description: Other 7501 records by id (programs reporting on several things).

reported.description: Whether the program ever sent a 7501 report.

rm.description: Removed right after it exits (once a waiting parent has the exit code).

screen.description: "exact", or "inexact" after a core crash (older history may be missing).

status.description:
The program's own word for what it's doing (OSC 7501 root record);
null if it never said, or after it exited.

status_ms.description: When that word last changed, ms since the epoch; null if it never said.

submit.description:
Template overrides: the key that submits a message, the stop key, the pause
between paste and submit.

turn.description: Goes up each time the status leaves `working`.

children.description: With `children`: one result per child it reports on.

ended.description: False on timeout: a check-in, the terminal is still running.

from.description:
With a message: the sender's address (the text is already in your input);
null when a person sent it.

reason.description:
status, exit (including program loss in a kept terminal), output, timeout,
or not_started (after a send: it did not start working; a plain wait
still follows that send's turn); with
`children`: children; message (someone messaged the waiter, any
wait); for each child in `children`: status, exit, or running (still
working).

status.description: The exact word the program reported (current word on timeout or output).
